RC365 Holding plc
("RC365", the "Company" or the "Group")
Launch of Banking Virtual Account Services in Latin America
RC365 Holding plc (LSE: RCGH), an established payment solutions and fintech company, is pleased to announce that the Group has enabled its Banking Virtual Account ("BVA") services in Latin America. The services are now live on the Group's portal.
The expansion enables customers to open local collection accounts in six Latin American markets, supporting collections in Mexican pesos (MXN), Argentine pesos (ARS), Brazilian reais (BRL), Peruvian soles (PEN), Colombian pesos (COP) and Costa Rican colón (CRC).
The BVA services are supported by six local banking partners: Hey Banco in Mexico, Banco Industrial S.A. (BIND) in Argentina, FITS Instituição de Pagamento in Brazil, Alfin Banco in Peru, Kamin in Colombia and Ridivi in Costa Rica.
The Group's BVA services operate through a business-to-business-to-consumer ("B2B2C") model and are delivered via RC365's software-as-a-service ("SaaS") platform. This enables RC365's business partners to integrate local virtual account and collection functionality into their own customer offerings and provide such services to their end customers. The launch in Latin America gives partners a wider choice of local collection options across six markets, supporting their ability to expand their services and address customer demand in the region.
Chi Kit (Michael) Law, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of RC365, commented:
"We are pleased to launch our Banking Virtual Account services in Latin America, extending our offering into six new markets.
"This expansion broadens the geographic reach of our payment services and provides customers with greater access to local collection solutions across Latin America. We look forward to building on this initial rollout as we continue to expand the Group's international offering."

Financial Services Award
RC365 Holding plc (LSE: RCGH), an established payment solutions and fintech company, is pleased to announce that its wholly owned Hong Kong subsidiary, Regal Crown Technology Limited ("RCTECH"), has been selected as the recipient of the Excellence in One-Stop Fintech Institution award at the Financial Services Awards of Excellence 2026.
RCTECH was selected following a rigorous selection process conducted by a judging panel comprising industry professional bodies, chambers of commerce and the organiser, Hong Kong Economic Journal Company Limited. The award will be presented at an awards ceremony in Hong Kong on 10 September 2026.
Chi Kit (Michael) Law, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of RC365, commented:
"We are delighted that RCTECH has been recognised with the Excellence in One-Stop Fintech Institution award. This recognition reflects the continued efforts of our team to develop and deliver integrated financial technology and payment solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers.
"The award is also an encouraging endorsement of the capabilities we have built within the Group as we continue to broaden our fintech offering and pursue our growth strategy across our target markets. I would like to thank the RCTECH team for their contribution to this achievement."

company_30s.what_they_do: RCGH is a tech‑focused firm that builds and sells cloud‑based financial and retail solutions. Their flagship products include a next‑generation wealth‑management platform, a point‑of‑sale system for travel and hospitality merchants, and a modular app called RC3.0 that integrates payments, data analytics and customer engagement tools.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company is positioned in a market that is rapidly moving toward digital, subscription‑based financial services. Its products target medium‑size banks, travel operators and fintech startups that need low‑cost, scalable infrastructure. By offering an all‑in‑one suite, RCGH cuts deployment time and reduces vendor lock‑in, giving it a competitive edge over siloed providers.
company_30s.current_state: RCGH has recently shifted from a fundraising‑heavy phase to a product‑rollout strategy. The latest series of RNS show new credit lines, partnership agreements and the launch of its wealth‑management and POS systems. The business is still in the early revenue‑generation stage, with cash burn supported by recent placements. The stock sits far below its 52‑week high, reflecting a steep pullback that many investors see as a capitulation event.

rns_narrative: Funding & Capital Structure: Over the last two months RCGH has secured a £2m credit facility, completed a convertible loan note, and announced a new placing to shore up liquidity.
Product & Partnership Roll‑Out: The company has launched its RC3.0 app and a wealth‑management system, and entered agreements with Blacksilver Trust and PyWave Network to expand its ecosystem.
Operational Milestones: Key merchant POS deals with StarCruises and a soft launch of the RC3.0 platform signal that the firm is moving from development to deployment.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Silent but hopeful – traders are watching for a breakthrough launch while remaining largely indifferent.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the new credit line and partner deals as evidence that the company is gaining traction and that the platform is ready for market adoption.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the heavy reliance on debt and the lack of current revenue make the business fragile; they fear the company may struggle to convert its tech into cash flow.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Over the past week sentiment has moved from neutral to cautiously optimistic, but the volume of posts is still very low, indicating a lack of conviction on either side.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – no recent spikes in public interest, which means any positive news could trigger a surprise rally.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the RC3.0 soft launch and first paying customers – a clear sign that the product is production‑ready.
Announcement of a revenue‑generating partnership with a major travel operator, which would validate the POS solution.
Any positive update on the credit facility, such as a lower interest rate or extended maturity, would improve the company’s cash runway.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained uptick in daily volume that exceeds the 3‑month average, a break above the 20‑day moving average, and a press release that confirms customer sign‑ups or revenue commitments.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early to mid‑stage of a crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score indicates a tight compression, suggesting that the market is ready for a breakout once a catalyst confirms that the business can generate cash.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: RCGH’s deep pullback has removed the majority of weak hands, leaving only those willing to hold for a long‑term upside. The company’s recent funding and product launches show that it is moving from a capital‑raising phase to a revenue‑generating phase. If the stock recovers to the middle of its 52‑week range, the upside is roughly double the current price, delivering a 100% return on the risk of a full rebound.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is that the company cannot convert its technology into real revenue before its liquidity dries out. A failure to secure new merchant sign‑ups or a downgrade of the credit facility could trigger a further decline to the low‑point of the current range, wiping out the remaining upside.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: ~2× the current price if it reaches the 52‑week mid‑point. Potential downside: a complete loss of the remaining equity if the company runs out of cash or is forced to cut the product roadmap. The asymmetry favors the upside because the downside is capped by the liquidation of the remaining shares.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the 20‑day moving average, sizing the position so that a 10% move up would represent a 20% return. Place a stop just below the recent low to protect against a brief retracement. Use a trailing stop once the price breaks above the 50‑day moving average to lock in gains.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a confirmed volume spike of at least 150% of the 3‑month average coupled with a press release announcing customer contracts or a revenue milestone. This is the event that would trigger a long entry.
playbook.if_passing: If the company announces a debt restructuring that pushes the debt-to-equity ratio above 5:1, or if a regulatory body flags the platform for compliance issues, consider walking away. Those events would signal a terminal risk that outweighs the upside.

ai_insights.bottom_line: RCGH is a deeply discounted tech platform that just finished a major funding round and is rolling out its flagship product; the lack of public chatter and a tight market compression create a prime contrarian play with high upside if the product gains traction.
